main_topics.reason: The user described a three-week flare with thick scale at the crown and patches around the hairline and ears.
The user asked what treatment comes after shampoos and discussed steroid preparations, calcipotriol, and softening the scale.
The user said tar and ketoconazole shampoos were no longer helping and later noted they were the only treatments provided.
The user asked whether scalp steroids are safe because they had heard steroids can thin skin.
The user asked whether to return to a GP or see a dermatologist and noted long waits for dermatology appointments in France.
The user asked for help with nighttime itch, said avoiding scratching would be hard, and asked about the Koebner term.
The user said visible flakes falling on their shoulders were embarrassing at work.

output.summary: The user described a persistent scalp psoriasis flare despite medicated shampoos, with thick scale, itching, and embarrassment at work. The assistant discussed scale-softening and prescription treatments, answered questions about steroid safety and calcipotriol, and suggested seeing the GP while waiting for dermatology; the user ended with a plan to book the GP, ask about treatments, use oil on the thick patch, and try not to scratch.
